## Agent containment (2026-10-03/04 night, Claude Opus 5.5 "TTYD Claude #2"; investigation Claude Opus 5.5 orchestrator)

- **What happened.** The agents' sandbox was `bwrap --dev-bind / / --bind $WS/tmp /tmp`: the whole filesystem
  writable, and the reaper killed only processes whose cwd was in the workspace. At least four agents wrote outside
  their workspaces over two days: a wave 54 kpaFireAttack agent left ~/new_kpa.c (Oct 2); wave 65's winMsgDisp agent
  made ~/permuter-msgdisp{,2,3,4} and ran its own decomp-permuter instances from the shared install (Oct 3
  12:58-13:21); wave 70's battle_camera agent copied its workspace 8 times into ~/par, started 16 detached
  `nohup python3 worker.py` searches outside the workspace, killed them with a host-wide `pkill -f worker.py`, and
  deleted ~/par afterwards (20:53-23:34). Its reasoning: "16 cores. I could run 8 parallel search instances, each in
  its own copy of the repo" (the wave rules reserved the permuter for others). Its load starved the permuter. 22
  other surviving sessions went outside without writing (mostly `cd` typos; two read ~/permuter's settings.toml);
  several ran nohup/& searches inside their workspace. Older sessions were pruned before they could be scanned.
- **Threat model.** Agents are not malicious, but they are resourceful and will take compute or paths the prompt
  doesn't forbid. Covered: writes outside the workspace; processes that outlive the agent (nohup, setsid, &); signals
  to processes outside the agent; CPU, memory and task monopoly; host services that act outside any sandbox (docker,
  whose group is root; the user D-Bus and systemd, which start unsandboxed units); credentials in ~; the
  launcher's own post-run steps, which ran agent-editable code and followed agent-planted links on the host; and the
  evidence (events, audit) living where the agent could rewrite it. Accepted: the agent reads its own key (it sits in
  its environment) and whatever the sandbox shows; its network is open (it needs the API). X11 is only partly
  covered: the X authority files are hidden, and the tower's X server refuses a connection without a cookie, but
  its abstract socket stays reachable without a network namespace, so that holds only while nothing like `xhost
  +SI:localuser` is set on the host.
- **Fix** (`tools/wave_launch.py`, now the versioned launcher; per-wave configs in scratch call its main()). Every
  step that runs the agent's files (the agent, check.py between passes, rel_link.py) runs in one sandbox:
  `systemd-run --user --scope --slice=ttyd-agents.slice` (CPUQuota 200%, MemoryMax, TasksMax per agent; the slice
  gets a runtime-only total of CPUQuota=1000% at launch) around `bwrap --clearenv --ro-bind / / --tmpfs $HOME
  --tmpfs /run/user/<uid>`, with /dev/null over /run/docker.sock and the system bus socket, only the agent CLI, node,
  the venv's python and the checkout's shared read-only parts mounted back under ~, the workspace writable, and new
  pid/ipc/uts namespaces (`--die-with-parent --new-session`). The sandbox's /tmp and the agent CLI's settings copy
  (settings and model list only; no credential store) live in ~/ttyd-agents-priv/<ws>, which no sandbox sees, and the
  host checks before every step that each writable bind source is a real directory, not a link. The key reaches the
  CLI through `bwrap --file` onto the sandbox's tmpfs, never a command line. The agent's stdout and stderr go through
  pipes into ~/ttyd-agents-out/<ws>; after the agent, `tools/agent_collect.sh` from the base (never the workspace)
  gathers final.c, the patches, provenance and the audit there, in a second sandbox that sees the workspace
  read-only, copying only regular files whose real path is inside the workspace; only that directory comes back
  (`rsync --no-links --max-size`). Collection runs after the reaper, and writes COLLECT-OK only if every step
  worked; `tools/merge_agent.sh` refuses results without it and a clean audit.txt (ALLOW_UNAUDITED=1 for results
  from before the audit). Disk: a host-side watchdog stops a step's scope when the agent's workspace, private and
  output dirs pass 4 GB, the event and stderr pipes are cut at 512/64 MB per pass, and collect copies files of at
  most 16 MB. Memory: MemoryHigh and MemorySwapMax besides MemoryMax (the tower doesn't delegate the io
  controller, so no IO weight). An earlier run's local results are moved to <tag>.prevN before a rerun. Every
  ssh/rsync has a deadline; the reaper stops the agent's scopes by exact name and kills only the known build
  programs in an existing workspace. Round 4: the disk watchdog polls every 10 s and also counts inodes; a failing
  `du` (an unreadable directory hides its size) counts as over; free space or inodes on the home filesystem under
  100 GB / 10 M stops the whole slice (deleted-but-open files don't show in du); once limits.txt exists no later step
  starts. An event or stderr pipe that hits its cap is recorded there too. COLLECT-OK is a manifest (sha256, size,
  name) of every file copied back, copied back last; `tools/collect_gate.py` checks a results folder against it (no
  limits.txt, a clean audit, nothing missing, changed or extra) and both `tools/merge_agent.sh` and
  `tools/adopt_agent.py` refuse what it refuses. ALLOW_UNAUDITED must name the folder and admits only one with no
  audit, collect or limits files at all. The audit flags a corrupted event log (an agent can append garbage to its
  own pipe through /proc). Slots are one pool for every key, so CAP and QUIET_CAP bound the tower's total. A failed
  reap skips the collect. The hard disk limit (ext4 project quotas or a loop image per workspace) needs sudo and is in
  the proposal for Isaac. Round 5 simplified what round 4 added: du's exit status no longer counts (files vanish
  mid-scan in any build); an unreadable directory is found with `find -type d ! -readable`. The floor no longer stops
  the slice: the first watchdog to see it creates ~/ttyd-agents-slots/PAUSED (why.txt says what tripped), stops only
  the scope holding the most deleted-but-open space (`tools/floor_stop.py`), and no launcher starts an agent or a
  pass until a person removes PAUSED. Collect runs in its own slice. The reaper counts a scope as stopped only if
  `is-active` says inactive or failed. Slots count active agent scopes, which agents can't create, not `pi`
  processes. The host appends a marker after every pass, and the audit allows a garbled line only right before the
  marker of a pass that timed out. The launcher writes LAUNCHED next to its results, so ALLOW_UNAUDITED (now
  wave/tag) never admits a folder it made. Event and stderr caps cover the agent's whole run. Archive retention stays
  with the existing prune cron. Agent slots are reserved under a flock on the host, shared by every
  launcher on the key; an unanswered count is no capacity. The prompt forbids background processes and copies
  outside the workspace ("if you want more parallelism, say so in REPORT.md and stop").
- **Evidence that doesn't parse commands.** The launcher records containers and user units before and after each
  agent (host_changes.txt) and runs `tools/tower_check.py` at the end of each wave: entries of ~ not on the host's
  allowlist (~/.config/ttyd-tower-allowlist, untracked because it lists the home directory), shell startup files,
  ~/.ssh and ~/.config/systemd changed recently, processes in the agents' slice or in a workspace outside a sandbox's
  mount namespace, new containers and transient units, recent write counts per directory of ~.
  `tools/agent_audit.py` stays as a hint, not a defence: it follows `bash -c`, eval, `$(...)`, find -exec, xargs,
  heredocs and python -c, resolves $HOME, ~ and relative paths against `cd`, and flags WRITE-OUTSIDE, EXEC-OUTSIDE,
  BACKGROUND, HOST-SERVICE and SIGNAL. Rerun over 90 sessions from waves 66-70, it found more than the first scan: a
  wave 70 seq_command agent edited another agent's workspace (seq_action_g1's copy of battle_seq_command.c), a
  win_item agent ran ~/ttyd-perm's perm_objdump.py, and wave 69/70 agents on party_hit and ac_gauge_timing2 ran nohup
  searches in their workspaces.
- **Review round.** #367's first version (read-only filesystem only) went through a red-team review, a correctness
  review and Codex. Its filesystem part held; the holes were the ones the threat model now lists, plus regressions
  against the previous launcher (no ssh deadlines, an unguarded reaper, other_changes.txt and include.patch formats).
  Proposed, needing Isaac: a dedicated agent user outside the docker group, and `--unshare-net` with an API proxy
  outside the sandbox holding the key.

- **Status after round 6 (2026-10-04 04:30).** Round 6 landed the disk floor's action (tools/floor_stop.py: only
  home-filesystem blocks, each file once, a scope stopped only above 1 GB and its results marked so the gate refuses
  them) and PAUSED as its own state (checked inside the slot lock and at launcher start; every launcher stops taking
  work once paused). #367 stays open for Isaac; the swarm stays frozen until he decides.
  - **Follow-up items done (2026-10-04):** (1) the disk watchdog checks directories for both read and search
    permission, and trips on du's "Permission denied" stderr while allowing vanished files; (3) pass byte offsets
    and exit codes live in host-only passes.txt, and the audit recovers embedded tool calls from malformed lines,
    flags malformed lines containing tool_execution_start, and allows only one truncated final line per timed-out
    pass; (6) the watchdog rechecks its owner after scans, before marking a limit or taking floor action, and trips
    after three consecutive failed scope queries; (7) either output reader reaching its cap immediately kills and
    stops the agent's scope and records limits.txt. These close the four soft-containment follow-ups; the hard disk
    quota proposal below remains separate.
  - **Accepted residual risk:** the audit is a hint and the sandbox is the barrier; outside paths held in variables
    or in attached sed expressions may evade the audit; the gate proves the copied-back files are consistent with
    their manifest, not who wrote it (the agent can't write the local results folder); one agent can pause every
    launch by filling the disk (availability only; resume is manual); archive retention is left to the existing
    prune cron; busybox applets may run commands the audit doesn't name; on btrfs the inode floor needs a guard; the
    collect step's text pipelines don't catch every write error.
  - **Needs sudo (proposal for Isaac):** a dedicated agent user outside the docker group; a network namespace with an
    API proxy outside the sandbox that holds the key; ext4 project quotas or a loop image per workspace, which would
    replace the soft disk watchdog and the pause and settle open items 1 and 7 properly; tower_check by cron.

## fadedrv linked (2026-10-04, Codex)

`driver/fadedrv.c` now links with all 27 functions at 100% and all 32 checksums passing. A deferred unused pi helper between `disp_maku` and `disp_tec` pools pi before half/180 without changing instructions. At EOF, an immediately generated u32-to-f32 helper flushes deferred code before `force_active` and the `.rodata`/`.data` tail words; the linker strips both helper bodies. The const `lbl_802C1538` then lands at exactly 0x802C1538. Texture padding uses u8/u16/u32[7] to avoid introducing alignment; `.sbss` and `.sbss2` each need one gap word (the first `.sbss2` word is already a compiler-generated zero GXColor). All data section bytes/sizes match; `.sdata` and `.sbss2` objdiff scores are imperfect because their source objects partition the padding differently.

## Codex's wins, and why each worked (2026-10-04)

Every hard problem routed to Codex (gpt-6.1-sol, high effort, CLI `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`) was one
that cheaper methods had failed: Claude #3 by hand, swarm agents, and the permuter. Seven runs, seven results. Each
row: the blocker, what Codex found, and the reusable lesson. The full attempt logs, including what did NOT work, are
in `docs/codex/`; read them before retrying a similar unit.

| Unit (PR) | Tokens | Blocker before | What fixed it | Reusable lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| battle_unit (#374) | 156k | BtlUnit_snd_se_pos and pool order | s16-annotated temporary; literal floats; also corrected a wrong sentinel (-250000000.0f) in 20 setters | a "fix" can uncover a wrong value; checksum it |
| windowdrv (#375) | 150k | windowDispGX_System 99.97%, link failed | X FIFO write before y3 setup; `math_ext.h` + `__fabsf` drops 32 B of math-header doubles; one shared const GXColor; reversed .sbss declarations + gap word; NO trailing .data padding (MWCC emits it before jump tables) | math.h statics, shared colour constants, reversed .sbss order |
| koopa (#376) | 176k | i2f double pooled after a string in a deferred unit | an unused helper doing an int->float conversion, generated first with `#pragma defer_codegen off` ... `reset`, pools the double early; the linker strips the body | the "conversion double before strings" recipe in AGENT_BRIEF |
| eff_kemutest (#397) | 208k | .sdata2 2.0/0.5 order (inner-loop-only hoist) | assign the hoisted values in a block INSIDE the inner loop, just before GXBegin, so MWCC hoists them to the inner-loop preheader only; string NUL tail; unit-owned zero colour template in .sbss2 | block-scoped assignment controls how far MWCC hoists |
| eff_fire (#404) | 148k | all functions 100%, DOL differed; 2 Claude failures | removed 6 duplicate .sdata2 constants (values the original merges) while keeping runtime products and registers via locals, fixed pool order, reversed .sbss2 scratch declarations | DUP_OURS in sdata2_diff = we pool a value twice; .sbss/.sbss2 declarations often reversed |
| fadedrv (#406) | 161k | pi pool order + unreferenced .rodata tail word; 3 failures | an unused pi helper placed between disp_maku and disp_tec pools pi early; at EOF an immediately generated u32->f32 helper flushes deferred code ahead of force_active tail words, so tail objects land last | helpers can position pool entries AND force tail data placement in deferred units |
| fontmgr fontmgrTexSetup (#408) | 103k | register swap after ~27 variants (Claude #3 with mwcc-debugger) | rounded size assigned inside __memAlloc's argument (keeps size in r4, gives dvd/rounded r31/r30); block scan moved to an inline helper (header/i get r8/r6) | assignment-in-argument and inline helpers change web ranks where declaration order can't |
| eff_kemuri (not linked) | 425k | 41 named .sdata2 floats reloaded in loops; 2 swarm failures | MISS: .rodata/.data/.sbss2 now byte-identical and the unit owns its data; 4 anonymous literals (20, 0.5, 6.4, 1/128) still pool at the tail instead of among the named floats | defining data before the functions fixes the pool but propagates initialisers into code; immediate helpers flush ALL deferred code at once, so they can't interleave single entries |
| mot_plane (#431) | 301k | DUP_OURS x9 in .sdata2; 2 swarm failures | removed nine duplicate constants with guarded locals keeping registers, and fixed pool order with two deferred helpers (19/40 experiments) | the eff_fire recipe transfers: brief it explicitly |
| eff_recovery (#435) | 144k | DUP_OURS x1 (0.5); .sdata2 object order; 2 swarm failures | merged the duplicate 0.5, positioned the pool prefix before the named 108, removed padding that shifted four switch jump tables | padding objects can move jump tables: check jumptable addresses when a data pad is added |
| mot_ship (partial, not linked) | 263k | .sdata2 91.8% + mot_ship 99.76%; 2 swarm failures | .sdata2 byte-identical via pool helpers and expression order; mot_ship 99.76 -> 99.89 via float-load fixes; 39 integer-register differences remain (38/40 experiments) | a data gap often closes with the function's pool; registers need mwccdbg |
| eki_00 ext_moamoa_main (partial) | 257k | constant addressing after the union fix | 97.04 -> 97.29 (244 -> 204 instruction diffs): constant loading, vector register/stack order, the rider-vector tail; float-register allocation, operand order and random-range scheduling remain; two helpers (ext_moamoa_init 99.38, moamoa_hit_check 97.25) also unmatched | the unit was never a single-function unit: check the whole unit before routing a link |
| ext_moamoa_main x3, res==3 block (partial) | ? | ~10 instructions of scheduling at the res==3 block top; Claude #3's 2 attempts failed | named angle inputs and an earlier `half` initialisation fix load order and float registers in all three copies: eki_00 97.293 -> 97.298, rsh_05 95.00 -> 95.20, rsh_06 90.50 -> 90.71; the vec3 address hoist, the breath input register and a delayed multiply remain (25/25 experiments) | one copyable shape moved all three copies |
| eff_ultra_hammer N_systemErrorHandler (partial) | 197k | error-handler registers, frame and unsigned conversions; earlier run 96.75% | 96.75 -> 97.53: explicit unsigned conversion reusing the existing mask at str_803019E0+0x190 and reordered match-only locals recover most registers and the frame; fsub+frsp vs fsubs, conversion slot placement (0x20 vs 0x14e0) and an r30/r31 swap remain; native literal pooling reached 98.92% but added 408 bytes of .rodata, so it was rejected (30/30 experiments) | a higher function score that costs data bytes is not progress toward a link |

eff_kemuri, later finding (2026-10-05, Claude #4, nothing committed): the .sdata2 ORDER is fixable. Define the four tail
literals (20, 0.5, 6.4, 0.0078125) as `const f32` objects in their retail slots among the other 41 definitions at the end of
the file, drop the header's extern for float_0p0078125 (only kemuri.c uses it), and have the code read them by name: .sdata2
and .rodata both read IDENTICAL. The cost is FPR ranking in three functions (effKemuriMain 99.64, effKemuriDisp 99.84,
effKemuri2Disp 99.85): a literal-initialised local outranks the hoisted int->double magic (which then gets f29, as in retail),

question is a spelling that makes a named-load local outrank a hoisted compiler temp: a mwccdbg/permuter job.

diff, tools to use, what already failed, MUST_MATCH rule, never regress). Each brief is in the PR's worktree as
CODEX_TASK.md; the template lives in the orchestrator's notes. Typical run: 12-25 minutes, 100-210k tokens.

## The compiler debugger's first direct win: evt_bero linked (2026-10-04)

`tools/mwccdbg.py` (cadmic/mwcc-debugger run in place on the tower; our wrapper and `tools/rasim.py` adapted from
mitsevox/tw2004, CC0) dumps GC/2.6's internal state for one function, and `rasim.py` replays its register allocator
exactly. Today it went from Claude #3's tool to something the swarm agents use inside the sandbox (~/mwccdbg
read-only, #445; dumps in the workspace; network off, #446).

**The win.** Wave 79 (the clean re-run of the debugger pilot) took evt_bero_move_mario_speed from 99.83% to 100%, and
evt_bero, 52 functions, linked. The tool chain led straight to the fix:
1. `mwccdbg.py` summary: every named local already had retail's register; the wrong colours were three backend temps
   (f49, f50, f53). Triage verdict FIXABLE.
2. `rasim.py neighbors --fpr f49=f2 f50=f1 f53=f2`: BeroSX's web must interfere with a later Bero/Y temp.
3. `rasim.py search 49 53`: the order that gives retail's registers puts BeroSX's web before the conversion.
4. Fix (MUST_MATCH, natural form in #else): copy BeroSX/BeroSY into locals `bsx`/`bsy` at the point the search named.
The link itself also needed the pool/data recipe: a `defer_codegen off` helper flushing .sdata2 before its tail gap,
the .bss order (BeroID, BeroSW, BeroINFOARR) and a .sdata2 tail gap word.

**The pilot behind it (n = 5 each arm, wave 77/78):** agents with the debugger matched 1 and improved 1 (tou_gamen
99.39 -> 99.62); agents without it matched 2 by trial. Every debugger agent used it heavily (8-61 runs) and it always
reproduced the allocator exactly. Its consistent value is diagnosis: naming the variables and the reason, including
proving the cases with no source lever (a parameter that must outrank a named local; a backend temp ranked above all
named locals). Since then register-class tasks start with a debugger triage, and NO-SOURCE-LEVER functions go to the
permuter instead of another agent attempt.
- **Batch 30:** evt_bero linked (52 functions; evt_bero_move_mario_speed 99.83 -> 100 from the clean debugger re-run,
  wave 79: mwccdbg showed the named locals were right and the wrong colours were backend temps, `rasim neighbors` said
  BeroSX must interfere with a later temp, `search` gave the order, and MUST_MATCH `bsx`/`bsy` locals implement it;
  merged as the function fix first, then the agent's link preparation through scratch/wave74/link_regress.sh). Wave 80
  group tasks: winmgr +4 (the select_disp family; 36/37, select_main 99.71 left), battle_seq_command +3 (the

## Inline asm in game code: the exception policy (2026-10-04, Isaac)

Game code is C everywhere, with two listed exception classes. An asm function is allowed only when
`tools/asm_exceptions.json` lists it (file, function, `class`, reason with the evidence, approval, date); `tools/ci.py`'s
lint refuses new asm anywhere else in game code (`--allow-asm` stays limited to the ported libraries under
libs/metrowerks/src), and tools/tests/test_asm_exceptions.py checks every entry is complete and really is asm in its file.
- **`compiler-artifact`:** bytes the original compiler emitted on its own that GC/2.6 provably cannot produce from C. Under
  MUST_MATCH, with a C form in `#else` so the natural build stays C.
- **`original-asm`:** code that was hand-written asm in the original, shown by the asm itself (instructions C can't
  express, or dead loads no compiler would emit). Approved by Isaac as "fine for now, tidy later".
Current entries:
- `src/system.c` `memcpy_as4` (original-asm): the original's hand-written word-copy loop.
- `rels/gor/src/event/evt_yuuranking.c` `yuu_kesan_chk_copy` (compiler-artifact): an unreferenced checked entry ahead of
  yuu_kesan (`cmpwi r4,0 / bge yuu_kesan / li r3,0 / blr`); GC/2.6 never emits a frameless tail branch from C and no version or
  pragma in GC/1.0-3.0a5 produces it. Split out of evt_yuuranking_alloc's symbol in #456; the asm form brings it to 100%.
- `src/driver/effdrv.c` `effMayaSetGQR5`, `effMayaAnimInterp` (original-asm, Claude #4, #473): a computed-GQR5 quantiser
  and psq_l loads, including a dead load, which shows they were asm in the original.
- `src/driver/hitdrv.c` `hitSetGQR5` (original-asm, Claude #4, #505): hitCalcVtxPosition programs GQR5 from the map
  file's vertex fraction shift before each packed vertex's psq_lx reads; MWCC has no mtspr intrinsic. The natural build
  scales by 2^-shift in C (it skipped the scale before).

Library `.s` files (outside the game-code policy): MetroTRK's `__exception.s` (the interrupt vector table, which opens with
the "Metrowerks Target Resident Kernel for PowerPC" banner) and `targsupp.s` (four `twui`/`blr` file-I/O traps) were asm in
the original kit and stay `.s` in libs/metrowerks/src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN.a. They are linked from dtk's disassembly as is
(8020 bytes, code linked 55.43% -> 55.64%); naming the vector entries after MetroTRK's source is tidy-up for later.

## Overnight 2026-10-05: unit boundaries, text order, and what not to retry

- **A stuck near-miss can be in the wrong unit.** eff_ultra_hammer's N_systemErrorHandler sat at 96-97.5% through
  30 Codex experiments (docs/codex/eff_ultra_hammer.md) because its literal pool and base register belonged to the
  data-only orphan `unk_0x8025de70`: retail addresses the handler's strings from that unit's section start. Splitting
  the two handlers into the orphan (#573, Claude #4) linked eff_ultra_hammer and put the handler at 98.96 in plain C.
  When a function's pool is exactly an orphan data unit's contents, check splits.txt before tuning code. ci.py now
  reports a function that changes unit at an equal or higher score as `moved`, not as a regression.
- **Function order is a link blocker the scores don't show.** About 40 unlinked units had .text out of order
  (`-inline deferred` emits in reverse source order). tools/fn_order.py was rewritten (#543, #545, #562, #566, #568,
  #570) and reordered ~25 units overnight; `fn_order.py --all` lists what is left. Order also moves the literal pool

## decomp.me: what the community already solved, and how to use it (2026-10-08, Isaac + Claude Opus 5.5)

[decomp.me](https://decomp.me) is the matching-decomp community's shared workbench. A **scratch** is one function
packed with everything needed to compile it: the target assembly, a context header, the C, and a compiler with
flags. Anyone can fork a scratch, edit the C and watch the score live; a score of **0 means matched**. Projects
register **presets** (compiler + flags) so scratches for a game start from the right settings. Hard functions are
usually cracked there by people trading forks.

### What exists for TTYD

- **Presets:** id 68 "The Thousand-Year Door (DOL)" and id 134 "(REL)", both by NWPlayer123. Preset 68 uses
  `mwcc_247_108` with `-fp hard -fp_contract on -enum int -O4,p -sdata 48 -sdata2 6 -rostr -multibyte
  -use_lmw_stmw on -inline auto,deferred -Cpp_exceptions off`. Our `objdiff.json` scratch block says
  `mwcc_247_107`; check which id is our GC/2.6 before setting `config.scratch_preset_id` in configure.py.
- **Scratches:** 232 carry the TTYD presets (140 matched), mostly functions we had already matched. A name search
  over all 292 functions still open on 2026-10-08 found 25 GameCube scratches covering 11 of them.
- **The people:** NWPlayer123 (about 135 TTYD scratches), Rainchus, theKidOfArcrania, SwareJonge, SplaatSites,
  fraser125, Cuyler36, kiwi515, SeekyCt. A hard TTYD scratch posted under the preset reaches them.

### What it gave us

| Function | Ours before | decomp.me | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `evt_eff_fukidashi` | 99.19 | matched (theKidOfArcrania, scratch NwWJP, 2024) | 100, #629 |
| `__strtold` | 99.24 | matched (cadmic, lPWyY), on `mwcc_233_163` with another game's flags | to try on our compiler |
| `_mapLoad` | 95.06 | 99.17 (NWPlayer123, t9PZw) | to port |
| 8 others | | at or below ours | nothing to take |

### Lessons

1. **Search before attacking a hard function.** A stuck function may already be matched there, sometimes for
   years (fukidashi's scratch is from 2024). It costs one search per function.
2. **A scratch match covers code only.** decomp.me compares the function's instructions with relocations masked;
   it never sees the unit's pool or data layout. Port the shape, then re-check `.sdata2`/`.rodata` and run CI.
   For fukidashi, a literal `0.0f` had been rejected here earlier because of the pool order; with the scratch's
   other changes in place the data did not change.
3. **Port the whole shape, not the most visible trick.** Fukidashi needed three things together:
   `#pragma opt_propagation off`, the height in one local with 2/3 of it computed into a second local before the
   call (variable as the first operand), and literal `0.0f` arguments. The pragma alone: no change. The shape
   alone: 99.79. Without the pragma: 98.96.
4. **Credit the author** in the source comment, the commit and the PR (for example "Credit: theKidOfArcrania
   (decomp.me)"), with the scratch id.
5. **Our hard functions are mostly new territory.** No one has posted the 99.9% register ties that stop our agents.
   Posting them (`winMarioDisp`, `effKemuTestEntry`, `battleCameraMain`, ...) is a way to get human help; it makes
   the project visible, so it is Isaac's call.

### How to look things up

- The site sits behind a Cloudflare bot check: `curl` and the in-app browser get "Just a moment..." (HTTP 403).
  Solving that check is off limits. What works is Isaac's own Chrome through the Claude in Chrome extension,
  where the check is already passed: same-origin `fetch()` from a decomp.me tab returns JSON.
- Useful endpoints: `/api/preset?platform=gc_wii`, `/api/scratch?preset=<id>`, `/api/scratch?search=<name>`,
  `/api/scratch/<slug>` (source_code, context, compiler, compiler_flags, score, max_score).
- **Go slowly.** About 100 quick searches earned a rate limit (HTTP 429). One request every 4 seconds with a
  60-second back-off on 429 ran all 292 searches in about 20 minutes without a single limit.
- The extension refuses to return script output that looks like query-string data, which includes most C source.
  Read a scratch from the page itself (page text, scrolling the editor, screenshots) rather than working around
  the filter.

### Our side of the format

objdiff's "Create scratch" builds a scratch for any function from the `scratch` block in `objdiff.json` (GameCube,
the compiler and our full flags with `-DMUST_MATCH`). The same bundle (target asm, context, C, flags) is also the
right unit for our own hard-function tools: it compiles in a second and holds no project state.

## How to frame agent prompts: night 5 experiment (2026-10-08/09, Isaac + Claude Opus 5.5)

Question: does a time cap, a firm target, or pushback get more out of an Opus agent on a near-miss unit?

| Framing | Agents | Typical run | Tool calls | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: "2.5 h cap, report your best state" | 14 | 15-45 min | 60-170 | 4 links |
| B: "firm target: keep going until the unit links" (no cap) | 4 | 1 h 45 - 2 h | 170-380 | 6 links (las_05, eki_00, rsh_05, gor_03, tou_03, battle_stage) |
| Pushback on a finished B agent ("one add away, keep going") | 1 | +1 h 15 | 57 + a 70-min mwsearch | no gain (aji_17 stays 99.97) |

- A cap is read as a ceiling but agents stop at their first plateau anyway: every A agent quit far below its cap.
- The same function under both: las_05 senkaron_ext_main stopped at 98.69 after 25 min under A and linked after 1 h 44 under B. The moamoa and gor_03 units went the same way.
- B costs about 3-5x the tokens per agent (290-684k vs ~100-300k); tonight it was the right trade (6 links from 4 agents vs 4 from 14). Budget accordingly: four B agents plus two dedicated sessions used ~5% of the weekly limit in two hours.
- Pushback adds effort but does not beat a residual that is genuinely stuck at the compiler level. It did pay off in Isaac's Codex run on rsh_06 (90.88 -> 94.83, "aim for 95%") where the source structure was still wrong, and that run's lead (make both rand() calls before scaling either) then let a B agent link eki_00 and rsh_05.
- Default from now on: firm target per agent, no cap; keep a usage heartbeat; push back once when an agent stops short with structural differences left, not when only a register tie remains.
- Not tested yet: firm target plus a minimum working time.

Also from the night: tools/mwsearch.py (#644/#645/#647) found two real fixes in seconds (evt_ryushi_clr via `*args++`, hei_10 npc_jump via `/ 2.0f`) but nothing in a 30-function batch of pure register ties; dedicated sessions (Claude #2, #4) with history worked well alongside subagents, but they must not share ~/ttyd-ci with the orchestrator's CI runs (concurrent checkouts killed each other's builds).

- **party_cloud** (Codex, branch codex-cloud, not merged): `.sdata2` IDENTICAL but `.rodata`'s magic landed after the
  strings; night 4 finished it with an uncalled original function (#615).

## Night 4: twenty links, and how each was found (2026-10-07/08, Claude Opus 5.5 orchestrating; Opus 5.5 agents, Codex branches)

Seven Opus agents, then a second wave of ten, all building on the tower (`scratch/tb.sh`). Code linked 57.75 -> 62.57,
data linked 86.43 -> 88.22, 20 units linked (#606-#624). Agent tags in brackets (claims n4/n5). Scores are from the PR
bodies; "comment" means the source comment states the mechanism, "PR" means only the PR body does.

**Register allocation and declaration order**

- **npc_event chain_main 99.93 -> 100, linked ([#606](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/606), Opus agent "chain").**
  The three chain-link passes had per-block locals named after their registers (`f28`, `f23`, ...); written over one
  shared set of locals (`x, y, z, sag`, the second loop reusing `i`), block 0's `x` gets retail's f28 instead of f23.
  PR: with per-block locals a compiler temp outranked `x`. Plain C. Earlier triage (night 2, Claude #3) had called it
  NO-SOURCE-LEVER, and a 14-minute permuter run found nothing.
- **ac_pendulum_crane_timing _get_angle_rate 99.20 -> 100, linked ([#607](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/607), "pend").**
  `angle = compAngle(0.0f, angle); angle += 45.0f;` instead of new locals `base`/`bumped`: the original reuses the
  parameter, which puts the sum in angle's f2 (comment). The 19 named `.sdata2` floats and `NF32`/`MATCH_F32` reads
  became plain literals in the same PR, which gives retail's `.sdata2`. Haiku 5.5 missed "reuse the parameter" in the
  morning benchmark; mwsearch later found it in 2.8 s (#645).
- **unk_0x8025de70 N_systemErrorHandler -> 100, linked (#607, "pend").** Index the buffer (`print_buffer[i]`) instead
  of walking two byte pointers: the original's two pointers are the compiler's strength-reduced induction variables
  and `&print_buffer[i]` its hoisted invariant (comment). The MUST_MATCH declaration split and an `extern 0.5f`
  workaround went.
- **unit_boss_moamoa ext_moamoa_main -> 100, linked ([#618](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/618), "smB").** All loops
  share `i` and the pose loops share `extPose`, "which is how the original's per-loop webs come out in its
  registers" (comment). Same family as #606.
- **sac_genki main_weapon -> 100, linked (#618, "smB").** Three `s32` field copies became one `Vec` copy
  (`eff->pos = genki->field_74`) after retyping the struct; a struct copy allocates differently from three word copies.
- **eff_stageclear effStageClearDisp 99.40 -> 100, linked ([#622](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/622), "smA").** Literals
  in first-use order, the 48/2 half extent computed at run time (`half = 0.5f; lo = -float_48 * half`) as the
  original does, and `shadow/work/j/i/type` declared in the order that gives retail's GPRs (comment). A `pool_i2f`
  helper, an `opt_common_subs off` pragma and a MUST_MATCH hoist were removed.

**Strings and constants as hoisted expressions**

- **battle_stage_object _object_fall_attack 97.10 -> 100, linked ([#612](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/612), "bso").**
  Retail computes the three sound names once, before the hit loop. `#define BSO_SFX(name) ((char*)(u32)(name))`
  under MUST_MATCH: "MWCC's frontend hoists an integer round trip out of the loop as an invariant expression; a plain
  literal is rematerialised at each call instead" (comment). Also one real wrong-code fix (loop 1 stores the entry
  index: `newEntry->no = i`, not `flag = 0`), per-loop locals, `*args++`, and the unit lookups nested inside
  `BattlePreCheckDamage(...)`. The PR body also calls two operand reorders "wrong code"; in the diff they are
  equivalent reorders. Night 2 triage had called this NO-SOURCE-LEVER, and permuter q32 only reached 2480.
- **evt_shop list_disp 99.07 -> 100, linked ([#610](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/610), "shop").** No `width` local:
  `FontGetMessageWidth(msg)` is called inside each expression, `msgSearch(...)` goes straight into `sprintf`, `i = 0`
  moves up to right after `pouchGetPtr()`, and `f32 w = FontGetMessageWidth(buf)` feeds the matrix x. No mechanism is
  written down beyond "retail calls it inside each expression" (PR). mwsearch could not reach it (#644/#645).

**Scheduling**

- **shadowdrv shadowCharShadowDisp_Projection 99.52 -> 100, linked ([#611](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/611), "shadow").**
  One late `fsubs`. MWCC cuts a long straight-line run into scheduling blocks of about 100 instructions. Reading the
  zero for each vertex's y through `#define PROJ_ZERO (*(const f32*)&float_0)` (MUST_MATCH; plain `float_0` under
  `#else`) makes the front end give each use its own load; the back end still merges them into one `lfs`, but the
  cut moves to retail's place, between v11's y and z (comment). `force_active` around the unreferenced `.rodata` vec3s
  and strings keeps them in the link.
- **eff_pointget effPointGetDisp 99.92 -> 100, linked (#622, "smA").** `#pragma opt_loop_invariants off` around Disp
  and two products moved into the outer loop, so the frontend's loop-invariant hoisting doesn't give them early temps
  in different FPRs (comment). Same lever as effKemuTestDisp in the brief.

**Data: dead strings, compound literals, function slots**

- **evt_mobj .rodata IDENTICAL (2576/2576), 79 -> 81/95 functions ([#608](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/608), "dead", on Codex's codex-mobj port).**
  The open question from night 2 (how does retail keep strings no code references?) answered: the original had event
  functions no map calls. MWCC pools their literals at the function's slot, mwld dead-strips the function, and the
  strings stay because live code reaches the pool through `...rodata.0`. Six plausible sibling event functions
  (`tornadoswitch_red`, `rideswitch_a/b`, `arrow`, `trap`, `bombrock`), with no float literals in them, replaced
  Codex's seven `pool_x()` helpers. Every experiment, including the negatives (`if (0)`, unused locals, uncalled
  inlines), is in docs/dead_strings.md. It also corrected the brief's "pool helpers can never link" (#613): uncalled
  functions are stripped; the real cost of a `defer_codegen off` helper is that it flushes deferred functions.
- **evt_cam evt_cam_shake 98.46 -> 100, linked ([#614](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/614), "cam").** Code: read
  `wInterpRelatedTime` as two `u32` halves joined into a `u64`, as it is stored; "a plain u64 load colours start,
  event and camId differently" (comment). Data: per-call-site `(Vec){...}` compound literals pool each template at
  parse time in source order (replacing the shared `makeVecByValue` inlines and ten placeholder objects), and three
  uncalled original-style event functions (`set_at_rel`, `set_npc_rel_str` whose `sscanf` supplies
  `"%f%f%f%f%f%f%d%s"`, `dolly`) supply the rest of retail's pool.
- **party_cloud N__cloud_use 99.90 -> 100, both pools IDENTICAL, linked ([#615](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/615), "cloud", with Codex's codex-cloud branch).**
  An uncalled `cloudSetMarioSpeed(s32 dir)` placed last in the file is compiled first in this deferred unit, so its
  0, 70, 180 and the int->float double head the pools; the linker strips it (comment). It replaced a named
  `double_to_int_*` that duplicated the compiler's own. Also: the `revise360` call passed straight into the sign
  condition keeps 70 as the first `fmuls` operand (match-only `s70()` gone), interpolation divides by `(f32)count`.
- **mot_jabara 98.86 -> 100, linked ([#609](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/609), "jab").** The repeated end-of-motion
  and camera-offset blocks became static inline helpers whose `(Vec){0.0f, 40.0f, 0.0f}` compound literals are the
  four anonymous `.rodata` vectors retail pools at parse time; dropping the `vec = &vec3_...` base also dropped the
  extra saved register (PR). The `return` moved after `jabaraFreeWork()`, and the `.data` gap object went (linker
  padding gives retail's layout).
- **mot_roll 98.55 -> 100, linked ([#621](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/621), "roll").** The same approach: the
  hand-written `Vec vec3_802c5d40[9]` replaced by compound literals in inline helpers and direct zero-vector writes,
  which pool first in source order; the `sqrtf`/45.0 doubles defined after `mot_roll` follow them (comment). Code:
  one local per quantity, float truth tests (`!f30 && !ay`) instead of a MUST_MATCH zero local, block-scoped `min`
  copies of `rollData[3]`. Two old `defer_codegen` pool helpers remain.
- **mot_ship 99.89 -> 100 and party_yoshi yoshi_use 99.46 -> 100, both linked ([#617](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/617), "ship").**
  mot_ship's repeated blocks are the original's helpers: `shipJumpDir`/`shipHarborTarget`/`shipHarborOffset` as
  plain static functions after `shipMove`. Under `-inline auto,deferred` they are auto-inlined into `mot_ship` but
  still emitted, so their constants (15, 50, 30.30303, 180) pool between `checkHarbor`'s and `shipMove`'s, and the
  linker strips the bodies (comment). That replaced four `shipPool*()` helpers. Which change fixed the 39 GPR diffs is
  not recorded. yoshi_use: plain string literals (no `"PYS_S_2\0PYS_H_1"` + 8 trick), two inlines, `.sbss` declared
  in reverse; mechanism not written down. `effSweatN64Entry`'s parameter order was corrected to the original's.
- **win_main winMain 99.99 -> 100, linked (#618, "smB").** Retail pools `"%s/w/%s/win.tpl"` (case 1) ahead of case 0's
  strings, which a case swap, an inline helper and an early static had all failed to give (ONE_FUNCTION_LEFT.md).
  The answer: case 1 calls `winTplLoad()`, a global function defined after `winMain`; in this deferred unit it is
  generated first, inlined, and pools its string first (comment). An uncalled `winFontSetC` sibling's `(f32)` conversion
  puts the signed conversion double ahead of `winIconSet`'s unsigned one, replacing `pool_i2f`/`pool_u2f` helpers.
- **seq_load loadMain 99.21 -> 100 and loadDraw 99.54 -> 100, linked ([#620](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/620), "seqld").**
  The window tables typed `WinDt win_dt[9]` and named directly, so `pool_data` creates the `.data` base at entry (fixes
  the r29/r30 swap); 38 named floats and strings became literals; `loadDrawVec` takes its template `Vec` by value, so
  its copy lands among each call's argument temps (comment); play time split through a `u64` local (no mechanism
  written down).
- **eff_kemuri: all six functions 100, `.sdata2`/`.rodata` IDENTICAL, linked ([#623](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/623), "kemu").**
  Main: `scale = touchdown_scale[..]; ... = scale * k` keeps the converted value the first `fmuls` operand. Disp:
  MUST_MATCH `opt_common_subs off` so the 0.5/20 loads stay separate until the back end merges and hoists them and
  ranks them like retail's literals. 2Disp reads 6.4 through a MUST_MATCH cast so the front end doesn't merge its uses.
  The four missing constants defined by name in their retail slots; `kemuriPoolFlush` removed. mwsearch later found
  effKemuriMain's form in 1.9 s with its literal <-> named-constant mutation (#645).
- **evt_win evt_unitwin_disp_func 96.53 -> 100, linked ([#624](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/624), "win").** Data: all
  `defer_codegen` pool helpers removed, functions in reverse retail order, dead `"%s_%04d"` from a reconstructed
  uncalled `unitwin_icon_delete`, named objects replaced by literals and compound literals, `char help[0x40] = ""`.
  Code: `dispCnt * 0x18` row offsets, which MWCC strength-reduces into a per-loop offset register (comment), instead of
  `dispOff += 0x18` accumulators; one function-scope loop counter; two static inline pickers. Two real bugs fixed (level
  up/down help arguments swapped). Three prototypes looked wrong and were cast under MUST_MATCH (FontDrawColor colour by
  value, FontDrawString `(x, y, str)`, iconDispGx scale first); see #627.

**Partial gains**

- **evt_yuuranking (yuu and gor) disp_func 98.18 -> 99.09 ([#616](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/616), "rank").**
  `fontlenpitch` walks by index (`msg[i]`) instead of by pointer: loop strength reduction then builds the pointer from
  `buf` after CSE has run, giving retail's two separate `addi rN,r1,0x78` instead of `mr r25,r24` (comment). One plain
  `fontlenpitch` matches standalone and inlined; the MUST_MATCH `fontlenpitch_inl` went.
- **battle_camera battleCameraMain 99.88 -> 99.92 and tou_02 ext_fan_main 98.86 -> 98.98 ([#619](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/619), "bcam").**
  `/ 2.0f` instead of `* 0.5f`: MWCC turns it into `* 0.5` with the variable first, retail's operand order (comment).
  `fanAngle` returns through a local: an inline's locals are numbered before the caller's temps (comment).
- **battle_detect BattleChoiceSamplingEnemy 100, _btlSamplingEnemy 99.95; itemdrv itemMain 100 (#618, "smB").**
  `_btlSamplingEnemy`: all locals at function scope in a chosen order. itemMain: `f64 d = __fabs(...)` temp; mechanism

- **eff_kameki_tornade_n64 99.69 -> 99.96 (#622, "smA").** All-literal pool, `i * 0x200` ring index replacing a

- **win_mario winMarioDisp 96.19 -> 99.99, `.sdata2` IDENTICAL ([#625](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/625), "wmar").**
  The `vp` single-base hack, `WM_*` macros and ~24 named Vec externs replaced by compound literals passed by value,
  literal strings and local tables (`GXColor colTbl[3]` inside the loop), so MWCC pools everything from one base with

## Haiku trial, prototype fixes, decomp.me (2026-10-08, Claude Opus 5.5; Claude Haiku 5.5 agents)

- **Haiku 5.5 benchmark:** 0 of 3 of the night's Opus solves reproduced (_get_angle_rate, list_disp, chain_main), even
  with the shared-locals hint; correct diagnoses and honest reports, but it stopped 3-8 minutes into a 90-minute budget.
  Verdict: gated mechanical work, not near-miss matching.
- **pmario_sound in retail `.text` order ([#626](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/626), Haiku 5.5).** `fn_order.py --write`, 40
  of 50 functions moved; the last unit that was out of order. calc3D 99.48 -> 99.47: its two int->float magic doubles
  were already swapped, and the move put the `"mri_00"` string past them, exposing the swap on both loads.
- **iconDispGx takes the scale first ([#627](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/627), Haiku 5.5).** Prototype
  `(f32 scale, Vec* position, s16 flags, s16 iconId)`, 147 call sites and the `ICON_DISP` macros. The original's callers
  evaluate the scale before the position, and arguments are evaluated in declared-parameter order (the intplGetValue
  rule). btlUnitItemDisp 98.02 -> 99.05, nothing dropped. The other two suspects were wrong: FontDrawColor by value
  dropped 25 callers that match with `&local`, and FontDrawString `(x, y, str)` cost gor_irai data; both reverted.
  About ten MUST_MATCH casts still spell the old order (battle_disp, sac_suki, ac_repeatedly, ac_lst_rc_keep,
  ac_stick_keep_left, sac_zubastar, battle_item_data); same registers, so harmless, but inconsistent.
- **goryuugijo_init_slot 99.17 -> 100 ([#628](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/628), Claude Opus 5.5, Isaac's call).** It returns
  `void` (retail leaves r3 unset) and is cast to `UserFunction` at its one assignment, as Melee casts callbacks.
  The permuter had reached 0 only with `void` on night 3. Same PR: the 12 reconstructed uncalled functions moved under
  MUST_MATCH with Melee-style `/// @todo reconstructed:` notes; plain builds drop them and their literals.
- **evt_eff_fukidashi 100, from a community decomp.me scratch ([#629](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/629), Claude Opus 5.5; shape by theKidOfArcrania, scratch NwWJP).**
  `#pragma opt_propagation off`, the height in a local, 2/3 of it computed into a second local before the call,
  literal `0.0f` arguments. Each piece was needed: the shape alone gave 99.79, without the pragma 98.96. The lesson
  (search decomp.me first) is in the decomp.me chapter (#630).

## Night 5: firm targets, mwsearch, and the first relays (2026-10-08/09, Claude Opus 5.5 orchestrating; Opus 5.5 agents, Claude #2 and #4 (Opus 5.5), Codex GPT-6 Sol)

Waves A/A2/A3 (capped) and B (firm target) as in the prompt-framing chapter; tools/mwsearch.py written and upgraded.
Links: evt_yuutitle, win_04, yuu_03, las_05, eki_00, rsh_05, gor_03, tou_03, battle_stage. Code linked 62.57 -> 65.22.

**Register allocation: what the frontend numbers first**

- **evt_yuutitle disp_func 99.80 -> 100, linked ([#632](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/632), Opus agent "yuu").**
  The fade as its own local (`fade = 0.8f * t + 0.2f; scale *= fade;`) under `opt_propagation off` for this one
  function (replacing `opt_common_subs off`): with copy propagation off the fade keeps its own low variable number, so
  the product is coloured first (f0) and the fade gets f1. The lerps carry an `(f32)` on the product, which mimics an
  f32 temporary in the frontend tree; without it MWCC picks a different `fmadds` shape (comment). rasim showed the
  product had to be coloured before the fade.
- **yuu_03 evt_ryushi_clr 98.37 -> 100, linked ([#636](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/636), "muj").** The TTYD
  idiom `s32* args = event->args; evtGetValue(event, *args++)`. The post-increment keeps `args` a real local, so the
  `xwp` address load takes r4 and the peephole no longer fuses `addi`+`lwz` (PR; rasim replay predicted it). mwsearch
  rediscovered it in 7.7 s once it had the `*args++` family (#647).
- **win_04 flower_disp 99.92 -> 100, linked ([#635](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/635), "maps").** The quad drawn from
  the texture's size: `f32 w = 101.0f, h = 92.0f;` and vertices `-w / 2.0f`, `h / 2.0f` instead of precomputed
  `46.0f`/`50.5f`. MWCC folds the halves but keeps the run-time negations, which gives the original's `fneg` temps and
  pool order (PR). No match-only code. mwsearch could not find it (a meaning-level rewrite).
- **mri_puni: evt_puni_set_lsw_index 98.27 -> 100, evt_puni_set_trap_index 99.36 -> 100, puniSearchRandom 98.90 -> 100 ([#648](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/648), Claude #4, Opus 5.5).**
  lsw_index: the slot index in its own variable (`base = index + i * 7`) instead of `index += i * 7`; retail keeps the
  two in separate registers. trap_index: `div` at function scope and `index %= 8` reused as the bit number (mwsearch's
  shape, rewritten as plain C). puniSearchRandom: the LCG written inline with its own local `v` instead of calling
  `puniQrnd2`. Declaration order for all three from `rasim.py search` against registers read off the retail asm.
  Same method: puniFukki 99.41 -> 99.79 ([#654](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/654)).
- **hei_10 npc_jump 92.18 -> 99.88 ([#641](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/641), "uran2") -> 100 ([#652](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/652), Claude #2 via mwsearch).**
  First rsh_05's three fixes from #631 (frame count through an `s32 ms` local, `PSVECDistance(&to, &from)`,
  `position.y += vy` before `vy -= grav`; no per-fix mechanism recorded) plus the three zero templates as the named Vec
  objects retail references (fixed the 0xc0 vs 0x90 frame). The last step, found by mwsearch in 1.3 s:
  `grav * frames / 2.0f` instead of `* 0.5f`. Same value; MWCC's parser puts the leaf operand of `* 0.5f` on the left
  and numbers the 0.5 load before the product, while the division numbers its operands the way retail's FPRs are
  assigned, which settles the dy/vy tie.

**Hoisting and the frontend: where a value is computed**

- **eff_particle effParticleDisp 99.22 -> 99.87 ([#633](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/633), "fx").** The half-size
  products written in place at each vertex (`GXPosition3f32(0.5f * -4.0f, 4.0f, 0.0f)` through the named reads);
  MWCC hoists them out of the loop in the original's preheader order 4, 8, -4, 0.5, -8 (comment). Removed the
  `top/left/bottom` locals and a match-only negate-half block.
- **las_05 calc_area 99.02 -> 100 ([#639](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/639), "las05") and senkaron_ext_main 98.69 -> 100, linked ([#649](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/649), "las05b").**
  calc_area: both differences, then divide in place, then convert (`dx = x - -570.0f; dx /= 40.0f; b = dx;`); the
  volatile MATCH_F32 read went (PR). senkaron_ext_main: the second loop calls `move_check` (auto-inlined) with
  retail's increment order, the two float products written in place inside the loop so the frontend hoists them with
  retail's priority, per-block `dx/dz/d`; the two sound names through a MUST_MATCH `KARON_SFX` cast, the
  `BSO_SFX` hoist again. The capped agent stopped at 98.69 after 25 minutes; the firm-target agent linked it after 1 h 44.
- **tou_03 screen_tev and battle_stage tou_gamen_screen_tev 99.62/99.74 -> 99.82/99.83 ([#637](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/637), "tev") -> 100, both linked ([#653](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/653), "tev2").**
  The two copies of the same retail function each had half right; swapping halves gave 99.8. The last 11 instructions:
  `base` and `col` written as plain copies assigned inside the inner loop under `opt_propagation off`, so the frontend
  hoists only `i/4` and `i%4`, the shifts stay in the body until the back end hoists them, and they are numbered after
  the body temps (retail's colouring); `row` evaluated before `base` (comment). rasim had checked 5040 declaration
  orders with none matching: the lever was when the values are created, not their order.
- **aji_17 noiseDisp 99.11 -> 99.97 (#653, "tev2").** The same loop rewrite. The last `add` operand order resisted a
  75-minute pushback and a 70-minute mwsearch; GPT-6 Sol solved it on night 6 (#656).

**Random-number blocks: evaluate the calls first**

- **rsh_06 ext_moamoa_main 90.88 -> 94.83 ([#646](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/646), GPT-6 Sol in Isaac's Codex app).**
  In each jump path the original makes both `rand()` calls before scaling either result: `ra = (f32)rand() / 32767.0f;
  rb = (f32)rand() / 32767.0f;` then `ra * (0.5f - 0.3f) + 0.3f` as the argument. That reshapes the whole inlined
  `randf` block (PR). The diff also reorders `tx2`/`ty2` and `rad3`'s operands, not mentioned in the body. The squash
  trailer says GPT-6.1 Sol by mistake.
- **eki_00 and rsh_05 ext_moamoa_main -> 100, both linked; rsh_05 npc_jump -> 100 ([#650](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/650), "moa2").**
  #646's lead plus: `randRange`/`randScale` inlines reproduce randf's `t * (max - min) + min`; `moamoa_jump`'s float
  parameters moved before the ints (MWCC evaluates arguments in declared order; GPRs and FPRs are separate files, so
  the callee ABI is unchanged); constant multiplies as power-of-two divisions (`/ 4.0f`, `/ 2.0f`, replacing a
  MUST_MATCH `half`); separate locals for split live ranges; a few commented reuses of shared float temps that the
  mwccdbg colouring needs. rsh_05 data: table terminator `{NULL, NULL, 0.0f}`, `Mtx mt` at file scope before the vec3,
  the defined jumptable copy removed. Before that, #631 ("moa") had made eki_00 ext_moamoa_init 100 by making the
  source vectors non-const `__declspec(section ".rodata") Vec`: "as const MWCC knows the values and reorders the copies"
  (comment); four volatile hacks went.

**Data, function slots and function signatures**

- **gor_03: data layout ([#638](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/638), "gor03") then slot_rotate_sub 99.41 -> 100 and goryuugijo_main_slot 99.15 -> 100, linked ([#651](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/651), "gor03b").**
  objdiff's 0.2% data gap was layout, not bytes: function order (pool entries follow it), `fall_rtn`'s position (its
  Vec initialisers pool at its source slot), a named zero that pooled first, a `float_45` extern that only exists in
  the extracted object, and `.bss` order. `main_slot` became `void` (retail never writes r3). Then a `SlotData` struct
  replaced the `*(T*)(data + 0xNN)` casts, which exposed a real bug (retail skips the rotation while a reel's wait

list. Links: aji_17, win_mario, win_badge, itemdrv, eff_booboo_n64, eff_radiation_n64, eff_kameki_tornade_n64,

**Expression shape the allocator can't reassociate**

- **aji_17 noiseDisp 99.97 -> 100, linked ([#656](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/656), GPT-6 Sol, Codex app, ~11 min).**
  After ~3.5 h of Opus agents and a 70-minute mwsearch run: the row offset in its own statement and the final index
  grouped as two two-term sums, `off = (k / 8) * 32; data[(off + base * 256) + (k % 8 + col * 8)]`. MWCC reassociates
  any 3+-term sum; two two-term sums it can't, so it emits the original's `add r4, r4, r31` with the base shift still
  in r31 (comment + PR). MUST_MATCH, plain form under `#else`.
- **win_root winKirinukiGX 98.44 -> 99.11 ([#675](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/675), DeepSeek swarm).** The same
  rule in the other direction: `x + (w - 90)` is computed once, a plain `x + w - 90` reassociates and adds an
  instruction (comment); reusing the dead local `yscale` avoids a recomputed sum.

**Induction variables: let the compiler make the counter**

- **evt_yuucounter disp_func 99.33 -> 100, linked ([#662](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/662), "yuu2").** Digit
  positions as `xbase + (f32)(i * 30)` instead of named `xoff += 30` counters: loop strength reduction turns `i * 30`
  into the original's offset temps, which are coloured after the named locals; the named counter took a higher
  register and pushed `work` to r31. Integer locals reordered per rasim. Plain C.
- **win_badge winBadgeDisp 99.91 -> 100 and badge_disp 97.47 -> 100; win_mario winMarioDisp 99.99 -> 100; both linked ([#657](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/657), "win6").**
  Disp callbacks take `void* param` with `WindowWork* work = param;` first, which fixes the parameter-copy order in
  both. `(f32)(i * 0x28)` instead of a hand-written offset counter (induction variable again). Pip texture via enum
  constants: MWCC makes `K ? / K+1` ternaries of plain integer constants branch-free (`cntlzw`), while enum constants
  keep retail's branch (PR). win_mario's menu reads via `((f32*)((u8*)work + 0xC4))[idx * 5]` for the add operand order;
  a function-local static for `.bss` order. Both compile without MUST_MATCH.
- **eff_kameki_tornade_n64 effKamekiTornadeDisp 99.96 -> 100, linked ([#659](https://github.com/IsaacGemal/ttyd/pull/659), "fx6").**

  its counter temp is created (PR); one shared function-scope `theta/s/rad/c` set (comment).
